MUVNA Pentagonal Gravity Distributor (58.35mm)
Achieve the highest level of puck uniformity with this precision tool.
For the professional barista, ideal extraction depends on a coffee puck that is perfect down to the microscopic level.
The MUVNA Pentagonal Gravity Distributor is a precision leveling tool designed to eliminate air pockets and uneven density in the ground coffee before tamping. Thanks to a gravity system that automatically adjusts to your dose, this distributor delivers the consistency needed to prevent channeling and unlock the full flavor potential of every bean.

Key Features
1. Unique 5-blade pentagonal geometry
The defining feature of this distributor is its unique five-blade base. While standard distributors only work the surface, the pentagonal shape creates more points of contact, efficiently redistributing coffee particles from the center to the edges of the basket. The result is a dense, uniform puck that allows water to flow evenly, producing a balanced cup with outstanding clarity, sweetness and rich body.

2. Self-Adjusting Gravity Technology
The distributor features a self-leveling gravity mechanism. The weighted base automatically settles onto the surface of the coffee bed, adjusting its depth to the volume and dose of ground coffee. This completely eliminates the need for manual calibration, saving you time and effort when switching between coffees or doses from 18 to 22 grams.

3. Commercial-Grade Quality and Elegant Design
Made from food-grade 304 stainless steel and aluminum alloy, the tool is built to last even under intensive commercial use. A stylish matte finish and ergonomic handle give it a professional look and provide just the right force for a perfectly level surface.

4. 58.35 mm Precision Fit
The 58.35 mm base diameter is engineered for a snug, gap-free fit in professional 58 mm baskets, completely eliminating unleveled coffee at the edges and ensuring maximum efficiency.

What is RDT?
In the coffee industry, RDT stands for “Ross Droplet Technique”.
RDT is a method in which coffee beans are sprayed with a small amount of water before grinding. It helps eliminate static and improves grinding efficiency and puck uniformity.
The RDT method was invented by Australian barista Ross Quail. A fine mist of water on the beans reduces static, allowing them to be ground more evenly. This process minimizes coffee dust and uneven grinding, ultimately improving the efficiency and quality of extraction.

Place the coffee beans in a container and spritz them evenly with a small amount of water. Stir gently so the beans are evenly moistened, then wait until the moisture has evaporated from the surface before grinding.
It is important to control the amount of water used. Excess moisture can affect the flavor and quality of the coffee. In addition, RDT is mainly suited to grinders with flat burrs or blades and is not recommended for grinders with conical burrs.

How to use
Place the beans in a tray or container.
Twist the head to open the nozzle.
Lightly spritz the beans once or twice.
Grind as usual
